messages:

Subject: Retainer details and on-call model questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the materials with our infra and SRE leads and had a couple of follow-ups so I can prepare for procurement:

- Can you confirm whether the retainer gives us an "embedded" on-call person (sits on our rotation and has direct Slack access) vs a "shared" Red-Cloud on-call? If embedded, is that an engineer dedicated to us or a named rotation?
- How do you amortize uptime credits and service credits? We prefer monthly amortization rather than applying everything after an incident.
- What pricing bands are available for 12 vs 24 month commitments, and do credits scale with committed tokens?
- Any standard exclusions to SLA credits (e.g. scheduled maintenance windows, customer-side outages) we should be aware of?

We'd like the proposal in writing; procurement will need an attachment they can share. Can you send a numbered proposal and a sample on-call schedule?

Appreciate it — aim is to close contracting in the next two weeks.

Best,

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 13:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retainer details and on-call model questions

Hi Samir —

Thanks — below is a concise initial proposal and answers so procurement has something to review. I attached the formal PDF (redwood_retainer_v1.pdf) and a sample schedule (oncall_schedule_example.xlsx).

1) Embedded vs shared on-call
- Offering: Embedded-sounding construct where we assign a named Redwood engineer into BrightLane's rotation for the duration of the retainer. For the first 6 months this is dedicated (dedicated embedded engineer). After month 6, we transition to a named rotation of 2–3 engineers who backfill as needed.
- Rationale: dedicated early-stage support accelerates runbook handoff and reduces time-to-resolution; rotation after 6 months reduces cost while preserving knowledge continuity.

2) Credit amortization and mechanics
- Uptime/service credits are amortized monthly against the retainer value. We calculate credits for eligible incidents that breach SLA; those credits are (a) deducted from the invoice for the following month, or (b) applied as a one-time refund if the contract terminates within the billing quarter (customer choice in contract).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (72-hour notice windows), customer-side network issues, and force majeure. We document incident adjudication within runbook and post-incident review.

3) Pricing bands and commitments (high level)
- 12-month retainer: 1.0x list price; optional 15% discount for upfront payment or revenue commit; includes 40 hours/month embedded support coverage + 24/7 escalation path.
- 24-month retainer: 0.90x list with 20% discount for upfront pay; includes priority scheduling and quarterly on-site review (if requested).
- Credits scale: credits available per 1M committed tokens; we provide a credits schedule tied to committed token bands in the attached PDF.

4) Next steps
- Attached: redwood_retainer_v1.pdf (formal proposal) and oncall_schedule_example.xlsx (sample rota).
- I can hop on a 30-minute call Monday to walk procurement and SRE through on-call ops and credit adjudication.

If this looks like a good starting point, let me know the best time for a call and whether procurement prefers a DocuSign route.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
